Points to Consider: The University of Rhode Island launched its Workday implementation on January 12, 2026, to replace its PeopleSoft Human Resources and Finance systems and the PBCS budgeting platform.
The project has successfully completed the Planning stage and is currently in the Architect and Configure stage, where functional and technical teams are configuring business requirements, validating system design, and testing configurations to ensure alignment with institutional needs.
Overall, the implementation remains on track across the majority of workstreams and continues to perform within planned timeline and budget expectations.

Project leadership and governance have remained stable and effective, providing consistent oversight and decision-making throughout the implementation.
State system integration remains the most significant project risk.
Identified early in the implementation, this dependency continues to present challenges because critical aspects of the integration effort are outside the direct control of URI and rely on State of Rhode Island stakeholders and timelines.
URI and the State of Rhode Island leadership team have been meeting monthly on the project status.
Change management continues to be a key factor for the implementation.
Over the past several weeks, outreach and engagement efforts have increased to provide opportunities for faculty, staff, and campus stakeholders to learn about the Workday program.
These activities are focused on building awareness, preparing the University community for upcoming changes, and driving adoption to support a successful transition to the new system .
Overall, the project remains on track , however we are mindful and maintain focus on risk management, stakeholder engagement, and organizational readiness.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Enacted FY2027 Budget Purpose of Submittal: To provide an overview of the enacted FY27 State budget, approved by the Rhode Island General Assembly on June 9, 2026. Points to Consider: • The final appropriations bill includes a $4.2M increase to the General state Appropriation, with $1.3M intended for increased central costs. • The bill also includes $5M in operating dollars as startup funds for a Medical School. • The bill includes $15.2M in RICAP Asset Protection funds, $1.6M in new funding for Access Control, $9.0M (over 5 years) to address accessibility related projects, and $21M (over 5 years) to address building envelope projects. The enacted budget includes all other existing RICAP projects appropriated as expected. • The bill restores most of the funding for the Integrated Health Building General Obligation Bond, which was requested at $165.7M. Though the Governor’s requested budget recommended only $105.0M, the enacted budget amount was $165.0M. • The bill also provides Kushner authorization for URI to issue revenue bonds for Repaving and Hardscaping ($20.0M) and Automotive and Administrative Services ($14.4M). • Finally, while not aligning with the Governor’s recommendation for the removal of the FTE cap for URI, the bill increased the FTE cap by 200, including a new auxiliary cap of 450 (inclusive of the University’s overall FTE cap). 2023-1.v2.04222024 RFP – Agency Solicitation Specifications Page 2 of 7 Revised 4/22/2024 SECTION A.
BACKGROUND The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated and qualified vendor to provide emergency and routine utility maintenance and repair services for all underground and above -ground utility systems , excluding electrical , located on the Kingston, Narragansett Bay and W.
Alton Jones campuses .
These critical systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water, natural gas, propane and heating oil.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
URI owned utility systems on the Kingston campus include a central steam plant, steam and condensate distribution/return network s, Five natural gas distribution networks, sewer collection system with four sewer pump stations, potable water supply and distribution, oil and propane fuel storage tanks for heating systems and a stormwater collection system.
The 153 acre Narragansett Bay Campus consists of 41 buildings and 326,000 square feet.

Utilities include natural gas supplied by RIE and distributed by URI owned piping network, potable water provided by the town and distributed by URI owned piping network, sewer collected by URI owned piping network and sent to the town for treatment, stormwater collection sy stem and oil and propane fuel storage for heating and generators.
The W.
Alton Jones campus is a rural campus in West Greenwich, RI and composed of 30 buildings.
Utilities include three small public water systems, septic systems, propane and oil storage for heating systems.
The selected vendor must have a thorough understanding of connection and repair methods for each of these utilities and an integral understanding of each of the university’s utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section B of this solicitation.
The vendor shall demonstrate troubleshooting of utility outages and methods of providing control of the utility network and temporary service.
As such, the selected vendor(s) will be required to study and understand the universi ty’s utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract’s award date.

The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide routine and emergency service for pipefitter, steamfitter and plumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
Services shall also include investigation as necessary to ensure proper repair (locating, camera work, transit level, etc).
For clarification, the University will continue to utilize the State Master Price Agreement for general plumbing (MPA #40) and steamfitter work (MPA #199) for repairs and maintenance outside of the scope of utilities.
SECTION B: SCOPE OF WORK AND REQUIREMENTS Vendors submitting proposals in response to this solicitation must demonstrate that they have the capacity, capability and qualifications to respond to emergency and non- emergency utility events and maintenance requests.
Vendors shall demonstrate and furnish the labor, materials, and equipment necessary for repairing underground and above -ground utility systems, including excavation, utility repair and site restoration services where necessary.

Utility systems covered under this service contract will incl ude steam, potable and non-potable water, natural gas, propane, heating oil, sewer and storm water infrastructure.
All materials used for maintenance and repairs to utility systems must satisfy code requirements and conform with the University’s standards for pipe and fittings.
These standards are provided in Appendix D.
Vendors shall

2023-1.v2.04222024 RFP – Agency Solicitation Specifications Page 3 of 7 Revised 4/22/2024 demonstrate they have the knowledge, skills and tools necessary to repair each unique pipe material, adapt to new pipe materials and an understanding of the repair principles required for each utility piping system.
Most emergency requests from the University are due to a compromised utility main or service line that directly affects its customers.
As such, vendors must demonstrate they have the capacity and knowledge to respond to an emergency service call within fifteen (15) minutes and be on site and properly equipped within one (1) hour of the request, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
This requirement includes ensuring the staff have the utility repair knowledge and providing the equipment necessary for responding to the emergency.
Emergency responses will include assessment of utility failures, consulting with URI utility staff, performing actions, as directed, to minimize impact to the campus population and damage to the utility systems.
It may also include temporary measures to return utility service until a permanent repair can be performed.

Vendors must demonstrate that they have all the response personnel, possess appropriate licensure and certifications for performing requested/required tasks.
Evidence of these credentials must be submitted as part of the proposal.
Vendors must demonstrate that they have access to well -maintained heavy equipment, shoring, pumps, lighting, tools, and materials, as well as backup equipment in the event of a breakdown during an emergency or scheduled repair.
The vendor shall demonstrate that they stock various materials of pipe and diameters used for each utility, fittings, valves, couplings, etc. used by the University to reduce repair time.
Pertinent utility systems information and service requirements: • Steam system on the Kingston Campus only operates at 100psi, 350 degrees F. o Vendor(s) will provide service up to and including PRVs in each building, as well as associated low-pressure piping beyond the PRV as necessary to ensure a proper repair. o The majority of steam pipe is manufactured by “Thermacore” and is of the jacketed insulated HT406 Type.

URI has since 2012 standardized on a Conduit Pipe-in-Pipe system and accepts products manufactured by Thermacore, Rovanco, and Perma-Pipe. o Maintenance and repair services shall include all aspects of the system including main and condensate replacement, steam pit maintenance, steam trap maintenance, condensate pumping stations, drip leg repair, valve replacement, and welding. • Water system operates at up to 100psi o Vendor(s) will provide service up to and including the building backflow preventer and isolation valves. o Backflow testing and repair of approximately 400 valves annually.
Proof of c ertification shall be submitted. o Maintenance and repair services will be required for various types of piping.
The majority of pipe is ductile, however cast iron, transite and plastic exist as well.
Pipe diameters range from 2-20 inches. • Natural gas lines are University owned and operated.
